paper.title: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration
paper.research_summary: This paper proposes an ensemble machine learning framework (ECSG) that integrates three base-level models—Magpie, Roost, and a newly developed Electron Configuration Convolutional Neural Network (ECCNN)—via stacked generalization to predict the thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds. The method achieves high accuracy (AUC = 0.988 on JARVIS), exceptional sample efficiency (requiring only 1/7 the data of existing models), and strong generalization in unknown composition spaces (e.g., perovskite halides, Li-containing oxides, transition metal oxides). Validation includes computational (DFT) and experimental case studies on 2D wide bandgap semiconductors and double perovskite oxides.

task.task_name_raw: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds
task.objective: Accurately predict whether an inorganic compound is thermodynamically stable (i.e., has decomposition energy ΔHd ≤ 0 meV/atom or ≤ 25–40 meV/atom under relaxed thresholds)
constraints: must work with compositional input only (no structure required)
must generalize to unexplored composition space

evidence.text: Predicting thermodynamic stability of inorganic compounds using ensemble machine learning based on electron configuration

The thermodynamic stability of materials is typically represented by the decomposition energy (ΔHd)6, which is defined as the total energy difference between a given compound and competing compounds in a specific chemical space.
Compounds with a ΔHd below 0 meV/atom were considered stable and are labeled accordingly.

stages.stage_name_raw: Collecting DFT-computed thermodynamic stability data from public databases
stages.stage_goal: Acquire labeled training and test data for compound stability
stage_output: datasets of inorganic compounds with stability labels (ΔHd ≤ 0 or ≤ 25/40 meV/atom)

evidence.text: In this work, we compared the performance of various models in predicting the stability of inorganic compounds on three large DFT-computed datasets, MP, OQMD, and JARVIS.
We collected thermodynamic stability data for 496 perovskite halides from the literature.
Initially, we compiled a database of 1333 double perovskite oxides.

stages.stage_name_raw: Preprocessing compositional data and encoding electron configurations
stages.stage_goal: Transform raw chemical formulas into model-ready inputs, including EC-based 3D matrices

evidence.text: The input of ECCNN is a matrix with shape of 118 × 168 × 8, which is encoded by the EC of materials.

The construction of the features for ECCNN is illustrated in Fig. 8. The first step involves identifying the categories of elements in the compound... one-hot encoding is employed... Subsequently, these subshell feature vectors are concatenated to form atom features with a length of 168... the number of atoms is represented by the third dimension...

stages.stage_name_raw: Assigning stability labels based on DFT-derived decomposition energy thresholds
stages.stage_goal: Generate binary stability labels from computed ΔHd values
stage_output: binary labels: stable (ΔHd ≤ 0 meV/atom) or unstable

evidence.text: Compounds with a ΔHd below 0 meV/atom were considered stable and are labeled accordingly.
we slightly relax the threshold restriction when classifying materials stability. Consequently, we utilize thresholds of 25 meV/atom and 40 meV/atom to assign stability labels in the data set.

stages.stage_name_raw: Training base-level models (Magpie, Roost, ECCNN) and meta-level model via stacked generalization
stages.stage_goal: Train individual base models and combine their outputs via a meta-learner to produce final stability predictions

evidence.text: We utilized a highly effective ensemble technique called SG to combine the predictions from these individual models for forecasting the thermodynamic stability of materials.
The base-level models include ECCNN, Roost, and Magpie, denoted as f 1, f 2, and f 3. The meta-level model is a multi-response linear regression (MLR), denoted as F.

stages.stage_name_raw: Benchmarking predictive performance across multiple metrics and datasets
stages.stage_goal: Quantify model accuracy, robustness, and generalization using standard classification/regression metrics
stage_input: held-out test sets from MP, OQMD, JARVIS, perovskite halides, Li-oxides, transition metal oxides
stage_output: AUC = 0.988 (JARVIS), ACC, Precision, Recall, F1, NPV, AUPR, MAE = 0.064 eV/atom (ΔHd regression)

evidence.text: In our experiments, the proposed model yields an AUC of 0.988 in predicting compound stability within the Joint Automated Repository for Various Integrated Simulations (JARVIS) database.

To further demonstrate the robustness of ECSG, we explored its performance on a regression task for predicting ΔHd... the mean absolute error of ΔHd in the test set is 0.064 eV/atom, surpassing other models in accuracy.

stages.stage_name_raw: Enumerating candidate compounds in unexplored composition space (e.g., perovskite oxides)
stages.stage_goal: Systematically generate vast candidate sets for stability screening

evidence.text: We constructed the candidate space of perovskites by enumerating all possible ABO3, A2BB′O6, AA′B2O6, and AA′BB′O6 compounds. In this process, we considered all metal elements up to Bi, resulting in a total of 67 different types of cations that could occupy A-sites or B-sites... After filtering for charge neutrality, 4,524,608 unique compounds remained, forming the candidate composition space.

stages.stage_name_raw: Applying trained ECSG model to rank and filter candidate compounds by predicted stability probability
stages.stage_goal: Prioritize candidates for validation by assigning stability probabilities

evidence.text: By setting the cutoff probability to 0.5, we identified 1,877,443 perovskite oxides predicted to be stable, substantially narrowing down our search range.

stages.stage_name_raw: Validating top candidates via first-principles DFT calculations
stages.stage_goal: Confirm predicted stability through ab initio energy computation
stage_output: DFT-derived convex hull stability confirmation for 35 compounds (25/35 matched ECSG prediction)

evidence.text: We randomly selected 35 compounds with stability probabilities greater than 90% (63 in total) for first-principles calculations to validate the accuracy of our machine-learning method.
The findings revealed that, out of the 35 compounds, 25 matched our predictions.
